findings.title: Negative-offset 'advanced pagination' branch will crash with ValueError, not optimize anything
findings.body: When `enable_advanced_features` is True and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code does `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative `start_offset` (and potentially negative `stop`). Django's QuerySet.__getitem__ explicitly rejects negative slice bounds with `ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported.")` - it does NOT translate them into reverse-order SQL. So any request that reaches this branch (e.g. a client supplying a cursor string with a negative offset, such as `0:-5:0`) will raise an unhandled 500 error instead of the claimed 'efficient bidirectional pagination'. The entire advertised performance feature of this PR is non-functional for Django ORM querysets, and the inline comment "The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" is factually incorrect.

findings.title: Shared BasePaginator.get_result modified for a niche feature, affecting every consumer
findings.body: The change clamps `offset` to `max(0, offset)` only for non-prev cursors inside `BasePaginator.get_result`, which is the base class used by `Paginator` and `DateTimePaginator` across the entire codebase (not just the audit log endpoint being modified). Previously, a cursor with a negative offset (constructible via `Cursor.from_string`, e.g. a malformed/tampered cursor) would propagate the negative start into the queryset slice and raise a Django `ValueError`. Now it silently resets to offset 0, changing behavior for every endpoint using this base paginator. This is a broad, unscoped change to shared infrastructure to support a feature that should have been isolated to the new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` subclass, creating unnecessary regression risk across the product.

findings.title: Possible AttributeError/None-access on organization_context.member.has_global_access
findings.body: `enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` is evaluated unconditionally. Due to short-circuiting, if `request.user.is_superuser` is False, `organization_context.member.has_global_access` is accessed. If `organization_context.member` can be `None` (e.g. for certain contexts) or the RPC member model does not expose a `has_global_access` attribute, this will raise an `AttributeError`, causing a 500 for any non-superuser authorized org member who passes `optimized_pagination=true`. This should be validated/guarded (e.g. `getattr` with default, or explicit None check) before merging.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates ~90 lines of BasePaginator.get_result instead of reusing it
findings.body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator` copy-pastes nearly the entirety of `BasePaginator.get_result` (cursor handling, hits counting, result trimming, cursor building, post-query filtering) and only diverges for the negative-offset branch. This duplication means any future bug fix or behavior change made to `BasePaginator.get_result` (including the clamp logic just added in this same PR) will silently diverge between the two implementations, which is a maintenance and correctness risk. The differing logic should be factored out (e.g. an overridable method for computing `start_offset`/`stop`) rather than duplicating the whole method.

findings.title: Misleading comments claim unsafe/incorrect behavior is 'safe'
findings.body: Comments state "The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" and "This is safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level". Both claims are incorrect: Django raises a `ValueError` for negative slice bounds (it does not support reverse/negative indexing on QuerySets), and permission scoping on the queryset has nothing to do with whether negative offsets are 'safe' to use for slicing. These comments will mislead future maintainers about both the feature's correctness and the reasoning behind it.

findings.title: Undocumented, unvalidated query parameter controls server-side pagination strategy
findings.body: `use_optimized = request.GET.get("optimized_pagination") == "true"` introduces a new, undocumented API query parameter that is not validated through `AuditLogQueryParamSerializer` and silently changes which paginator class (and therefore which code path, including the buggy negative-offset handling) is used. This is an unreviewed/undocumented API surface change: there's no serializer validation, no API documentation update, and the exact-string comparison (`"true"`) means values like `"True"` or `"1"` silently fall back to default pagination with no error, which is confusing behavior for API consumers.

findings.title: Negative offsets handled inconsistently with existing paginator conventions in the same file
findings.body: Elsewhere in this same file, `OffsetPaginator.get_result` and `MergingOffsetPaginator.get_result` explicitly treat negative offsets as invalid input and raise `BadPaginationError("Pagination offset cannot be negative")`. This PR instead attempts to actively support negative offsets in `OptimizedCursorPaginator`/`BasePaginator`, which is inconsistent with the established convention and, combined with the Django slicing restriction, results in an unhandled exception (500) rather than a controlled `BadPaginationError` (400) response.

findings.title: No test coverage added for new OptimizedCursorPaginator
findings.body: The PR adds a new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` class with a novel negative-offset code path and an `enable_advanced_features` flag, but no tests are included (or referenced) that exercise this class, including the negative-offset branch that is actually broken. Given this is new pagination logic affecting a security/permission-gated feature, the lack of tests means the crash bug identified above would not be caught by CI.

findings.title: No test coverage for new conditional pagination branch in endpoint
findings.body: The new `if use_optimized and enable_advanced` branch introduces a new execution path (superuser/global-access gated optimized pagination) in `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint.get`, but no new or updated tests are included to verify this behavior (e.g. that non-privileged users fall back to `DateTimePaginator`, or that the optimized path behaves correctly), despite this being user/permission-facing logic.

findings.title: Comment describes a feature that this diff does not actually implement
findings.body: The added comment claims "Allow negative offsets for advanced pagination scenarios" and that this "enables efficient reverse pagination", but the diff makes no functional change to `Cursor.__init__` (`self.offset = int(offset)` is unchanged). The comment is misleading documentation that implies new capability was added here, when in fact the negative-offset handling (and its bug) lives entirely in `paginator.py`.
